item.title: De Profundis: Oscar Wilde in Jail — Sun Nov 8, 1:30 PM — Soulpepper Theatre
item.description:
“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”
This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL
The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.
In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.
Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.
Onstage at Soulpepper Theatre for a limited run from November 3rd- November 29th

item.title: Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons — Sun Nov 8, 5:00 PM — The Assembly Theatre
item.description:
What would you say if you had only 140 words a day?
Discover Sam Steiner's play this November.
Presented at The Assembly Theatre in November 2026, Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons is part rom-com, part sci-fi, and part dystopian drama.
The average person will speak 123,205,750 words in a lifetime. But what if there were a limit? Oliver and Bernadette are about to find out. Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons imagines a world where we’re forced to say less. It’s about what we say and how we say it; about the things we can only hear in the silence; about dead cats, activism, eye contact and lemons, lemons, lemons, lemons, lemons.
Directed by Bonnie Duff (Assistant Director Jane Austen’s Northanger Abbey, Guild Festival Theatre; Playwright/Performer This Feels Like The End, Theatre Aurinko/Next Stage Festival) and starring Lara Lucia (The Drowsy Chaperone, Shifting Ground Collective; Brontë: The World Without, Guild Festival Theatre) and Jack Copland (The Moors, Riot King Theatre; Th

item.description: This talk has unfortunately been cancelled. The Continental Philosophy Research Interest Group is delighted to welcome as guest speaker Dimitris Vardoulakis, who was the inaugural chair of Philosophy at Western Sydney University. Some of his books include Spinoza, the Epicurean: Authority and Utility in Materialism (2020); The Ruse of Techne: Heidegger’s Magical Materialism (2024); The Agonistic Condition: Materialism and Democracy (2025); and The Logic of Living: The Materialism of Ancient Greek Thought (forthcoming). He is the co-editor of the book series “Incitements” (Edinburgh University Press) and the journal Philosophy, Politics and Critique. He is currently Vice President of the Council of the Humanities, Arts and Social Sciences (CHASS) and has served as chair of the Australasian Society for Continental Philosophy (ASCP). item.title: 🌰 Hogg’s Hollow Fall Walk & Lunch! 🍂! — Sun Nov 22, 11:00 AM
item.description:
Try New Things in Toronto! ### 🌰 Hogg’s Hollow Fall Walk & Lunch! 🍂
Join us for a beautiful fall walk through Hogg’s Hollow, one of Toronto’s charming historic neighbourhoods tucked away in North York. With its winding roads, forested trails, stone bridges, and scenic ravines, this area feels like a hidden village in the middle of the city — especially when the leaves turn golden and the air starts to feel like autumn.
We’ll explore the valley around the Don River West Branch, taking in the neighbourhood’s natural beauty and historic character. Along the way, we’ll touch on the story of James Hogg, the Scottish settler associated with the area’s early mill, and the tragic **Hogg’s Hollow Disaster of 1960**, when five workers lost their lives during tunnel construction.
After our walk, we’ll head to **Swiss Chalet** for lunch, because nothing says fall like comfort food and good company! 🍗

item.title: Early Modern Philosophy Research Interest Group (Raphaelle Dupont, U of T) — Fri Nov 27, 10:00 AM — Jackman Humanities Building
item.description: The Early Modern Philosophy Research Interest Group welcomes Raphaelle Dupont, a PhD student in the department. Her main research interests are in the history of philosophy, especially in the transition between late medieval and early modern metaphysics. Before joining the department, she completed her Master’s studies with a thesis on Spinoza’s metaphysics.
